In trained lifters, the mechanical strain associated with aerobic endurance exercise does not rise to the level necessary for mechanotransducers to switch on mTORC1 signaling (76). Indeed, aerobic endurance athletes display slight increases in Type I fiber size while showing a reduction in hypertrophy of Type II fibers (28). Even very intense aerobic exercise does not seem to confer a beneficial hypertrophic effect in those who are highly physically active. This was demonstrated by the finding that 6 weeks of high-intensity interval training resulted in a significant decrease in Type II fiber cross-sectional area in a group of well-trained distance runners (49).
